label: PYQ-style
stem: For a reaction the rate law is rate $=k[\ce A]^2[\ce B]$. How does the rate change when (i) [A] is doubled, (ii) [A] is halved and [B] is tripled?
model_answer:
*How much to write: two short lines of working each · 4 minutes*

Rate law: rate $=k[\ce A]^2[\ce B]$

**(i)** [A] doubled:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{rate}'&=k(2[\ce A])^2[\ce B] \\ &=4k[\ce A]^2[\ce B]\end{aligned}$$

The rate becomes <mark>4 times</mark>.

**(ii)** [A] halved, [B] tripled:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{rate}'&=k\left(\tfrac{[\ce A]}{2}\right)^2(3[\ce B]) \\ &=\tfrac34\,k[\ce A]^2[\ce B]\end{aligned}$$

The rate becomes <mark>¾ of the original</mark> (falls by a quarter).

:::tip Your answer must contain
- the new concentrations <u>substituted into the rate law</u>
- the <mark>factor</mark> stated in words for each part
:::

**Marks are lost for:** adding the changes instead of multiplying; forgetting to square the factor for A.
hint: Put the new concentrations into the rate law and take the ratio of rates.

stem: A first-order reaction takes 40 min for 30% decomposition. Calculate its half-life. ($\log7=0.8451$)
model_answer:
*How much to write: 8 lines: k first, then the half-life · 6 minutes* **Given:** first order, 30% decomposed in $t=40$ min, so $[R]=0.70\,[R]_0$
**To find:** $t_{1/2}$ $$k=\frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]}=\frac{2.303}{40}\log\frac{100}{70}$$ $$\begin{aligned}k&=0.05758\times(1-0.8451) \\ &=0.05758\times0.1549\end{aligned}$$ $$k=8.92\times10^{-3}\text{ min}^{-1}$$ $$\begin{aligned}t_{1/2}&=\frac{0.693}{k} \\ &=\frac{0.693}{8.92\times10^{-3}}\end{aligned}$$ $$\boxed{t_{1/2}=77.7\text{ min}}$$ :::tip Your answer must contain - 30% decomposed means 70% left ($[R]_0/[R]=100/70$) - $k$ with unit min⁻¹ - $t_{1/2}=0.693/k$ and the boxed answer in minutes ::: **Marks are lost for:** using 30/100 instead of 100/70; changing the time unit halfway.
hint: 30% decomposed means [R] = 0.70 [R]₀. Find k first, then the half-life.

stem: The rate constant of a reaction is 0.02 s$^{-1}$ at 500 K and 0.07 s$^{-1}$ at 700 K. Calculate the activation energy. ($\log3.5=0.5441$)
model_answer:
*How much to write: 6–8 lines · 6 minutes* **Given:** $k_1=0.02$ s⁻¹ at $T_1=500$ K; $k_2=0.07$ s⁻¹ at $T_2=700$ K
**To find:** $E_a$ $$\log\frac{k_2}{k_1}=\frac{E_a}{2.303R}\cdot\frac{T_2-T_1}{T_1T_2}$$ $$\begin{aligned}\log3.5&=\frac{E_a}{2.303\times8.314}\times\frac{200}{500\times700}\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}E_a&=\frac{0.5441\times2.303\times8.314}{200}\\ &\quad\times350000\end{aligned}$$ $$E_a=18230\text{ J mol}^{-1}$$ $$\boxed{E_a=18.23\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}}$$ :::tip Your answer must contain - the two-temperature Arrhenius equation written first - $T$ in kelvin and $R=8.314$ J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ - answer with unit kJ mol⁻¹ ::: **Marks are lost for:** R in kJ with Ea in J (answer off by 1000); T₁ and T₂ swapped.
hint: Use the two-temperature Arrhenius equation; T in kelvin and R = 8.314 J K⁻¹mol⁻¹.

parts.stem:
Calculate the rate constant with units.
**OR**
Calculate the initial rate when [A] = [B] = 0.2 mol L$^{-1}$.
parts.model_answer:
From Expt I: $k=\dfrac{\text{rate}}{[\ce A][\ce B]^2}=\dfrac{6.0\times10^{-3}}{(0.1)(0.1)^2}$ $=\boxed{6.0\text{ L}^2\text{mol}^{-2}\text{min}^{-1}}$

**OR**

$k=6.0$ L$^2$mol$^{-2}$min$^{-1}$; rate $=6.0\times0.2\times(0.2)^2=\boxed{4.8\times10^{-2}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}}$

hint: Compare two experiments in which only one concentration changes.
model_answer:
*How much to write: two lines each for (i) and (ii); working for (iii) · 7–8 minutes*

**(i)** Compare **expts I and IV** ([B] the same): [A] × 4 and rate × 4 ($6.0\times10^{-3}\to2.40\times10^{-2}$), so <mark>order 1 in A</mark>.

**(ii)** Compare **expts II and III** ([A] the same): [B] × 2 and rate × 4, so <mark>order 2 in B</mark>.

$$\text{rate}=k[\ce A][\ce B]^2$$

$$(\text{overall order }3)$$

**(iii)** From expt I:

$$\begin{aligned}k&=\frac{\text{rate}}{[\ce A][\ce B]^2} \\ &=\frac{6.0\times10^{-3}}{(0.1)(0.1)^2}\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{k=6.0\text{ L}^2\text{mol}^{-2}\text{min}^{-1}}$$

**OR** rate at [A] = [B] = 0.2 mol L⁻¹:

$$\text{rate}=6.0\times0.2\times(0.2)^2$$

$$\boxed{\text{rate}=4.8\times10^{-2}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- which <u>two experiments</u> were compared, and why (one concentration fixed)
- the <mark>rate law</mark> written out
- $k$ with its <mark>unit</mark> (L² mol⁻² min⁻¹)
:::

stem: For the reaction $\ce{A + B -> P}$, rate $=k[\ce{A}]^{1/2}[\ce{B}]^2$. What is the overall order? Write the units of $k$.
model_answer:
*How much to write: 3 lines · 3 minutes*

$$\text{Order}=\tfrac12+2$$

$$\boxed{\text{order}=2.5}$$

Units of $k$ for order $n$: $(\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1-n}\,\text{s}^{-1}$. With $n=2.5$:

stem: What is a pseudo first-order reaction? Give one example and explain why it behaves as first order.
model_answer:
*How much to write: 4–5 lines · 4 minutes*

A **pseudo first-order reaction** is <mark>a reaction of higher order that behaves as first order because one reactant is in large excess</mark>, so its concentration hardly changes.

**Example:** acid hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate:

$$\begin{aligned}&\ce{CH3COOC2H5 + H2O}\\ &\quad\ce{->[H+] CH3COOH + C2H5OH}\end{aligned}$$

Water is in <u>large excess</u>, so $[\ce{H2O}]$ stays almost constant and rate $=k'[\ce{ester}]$.

:::tip Your answer must contain
- the phrase <mark>one reactant in large excess</mark>
- an example <u>with its equation</u> and which reactant is in excess
:::

**Marks are lost for:** an example without the equation; not saying which reactant is in excess.
hint: Which reactant in a hydrolysis is present in huge excess?

label: PYQ-style
stem: Show that for a first-order reaction the time required for 99.9% completion is about ten times its half-life.
model_answer:
*How much to write: 6–8 lines · 5 minutes*

For a first-order reaction:

$$t=\frac{2.303}{k}\log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]}$$

At <u>99.9% completion</u>, only 0.1% is left: $[R]=0.001\,[R]_0$, so $\dfrac{[R]_0}{[R]}=1000$.

$$\begin{aligned}t_{99.9\%}&=\frac{2.303}{k}\log1000 \\ &=\frac{2.303\times3}{k} \\ &=\frac{6.909}{k}\end{aligned}$$

$$t_{1/2}=\frac{0.693}{k}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{t_{99.9\%}}{t_{1/2}}&=\frac{6.909}{0.693}\approx\boxed{10}\end{aligned}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- <mark>$[R]=0.001[R]_0$</mark> (0.1% left)
- both times as multiples of $1/k$
- the ratio worked out
:::

**Marks are lost for:** writing [R] = 0.999 [R]₀; skipping log 1000 = 3.

stem: The first-order decomposition $\ce{SO2Cl2(g) -> SO2(g) + Cl2(g)}$ is followed at constant volume. The initial pressure is 0.50 atm and the total pressure after 100 s is 0.60 atm. Calculate the rate constant.
model_answer:
*How much to write: 6–8 lines · 6 minutes* **Given:** $p_i=0.50$ atm, $p_t=0.60$ atm at $t=100$ s
**To find:** $k$ If the pressure of $\ce{SO2Cl2}$ falls by $x$, the total is $p_i+x$. So $x=0.10$ atm and $$\begin{aligned}p_{\ce{SO2Cl2}}&=p_i-x \\ &=2p_i-p_t \\ &=0.40\text{ atm}\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}k&=\frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{p_i}{2p_i-p_t}\\ &=\frac{2.303}{100}\log\frac{0.50}{0.40}\end{aligned}$$ $$k=0.02303\times0.0969$$ $$\boxed{k=2.23\times10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}}$$ :::tip Your answer must contain - where $2p_i-p_t$ comes from (one line) - the first-order equation in pressures - unit s⁻¹ ::: **Marks are lost for:** using pₜ instead of 2pᵢ − pₜ; no unit.
hint: Each mole of SO₂Cl₂ that decomposes adds one extra mole of gas.

parts.stem: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 298 K to 308 K. Calculate $E_a$. ($R=8.314$ J K$^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$, $\log2=0.3010$)

hint: Use the two-temperature Arrhenius equation with k₂/k₁ = 2. Where marks are lost: writing that a catalyst "changes the equilibrium" or ΔH; T in °C in the Arrhenius equation.
model_answer: *How much to write: one or two lines for (i) and (ii); working for (iii) · 7–8 minutes* **(i)** **Activation energy** is the extra energy that reactant molecules must absorb to form the activated complex (threshold energy minus average energy of the reactants). **(ii)** A catalyst lowers the activation energy by giving an alternative path; ΔG is unchanged. **(iii)** $k_2/k_1=2$, $T_1=298$ K, $T_2=308$ K $$\log\frac{k_2}{k_1}=\frac{E_a}{2.303R}\cdot\frac{T_2-T_1}{T_1T_2}$$ $$\begin{aligned}0.3010&=\frac{E_a}{2.303\times8.314}\times\frac{10}{298\times308}\end{aligned}$$ $$E_a=52900\text{ J mol}^{-1}$$ $$\boxed{E_a=52.9\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}}$$ :::tip Your answer must contain - (i) the words activated complex - (ii) lower Ea, same ΔG; a sketch earns goodwill - (iii) T in kelvin and the answer in kJ mol⁻¹ ::: **Marks are lost for:** saying a catalyst changes ΔH, ΔG or the equilibrium; T in °C.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Derive the integrated rate equation for a first-order reaction. [3]
(b) A first-order reaction has $k=2.0\times10^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. How long will it take for 8 g of the reactant to be reduced to 2 g? [2]
model_answer:
*How much to write: about one page: every step of the derivation, then the numerical · 10–12 minutes*

**(a)** For $\ce{R -> P}$ of first order:

$$-\frac{d[R]}{dt}=k[R]$$

Separate the variables:

$$\frac{d[R]}{[R]}=-k\,dt$$

Integrate both sides:

$$\ln[R]=-kt+I$$

At $t=0$, $[R]=[R]_0$, so <u>$I=\ln[R]_0$</u>:

$$\ln[R]=\ln[R]_0-kt$$

$$\boxed{k=\frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]}}$$

**(b)** From 8 g to 2 g: $\dfrac{[R]_0}{[R]}=4$

$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{2.303}{2.0\times10^{-3}}\log4 \\ &=1151.5\times0.602\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{t=693\text{ s}}$$

$$\boxed{t=693\text{ s}}$$

This is two half-lives of 346.5 s each.

:::tip Your answer must contain
- the rate law, <u>separation of variables</u> and integration shown
- the <mark>integration constant</mark> found from $t=0$
- final form with 2.303 and log
- (b) the ratio 8/2 = 4 and the answer in seconds
:::

**Marks are lost for:** skipping the integration constant; mixing ln and log; no unit on t.
